Only in Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour: God has created many jinn and humans for hell; The charge that a prophet is mad; The charge that a prophet is mad [response between the texts]; Having eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, said of idols or of people [divergence between the texts]; The prophet disclaims knowledge of the unseen and power over benefit or harm; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; To God belong the most beautiful names; call on him by them; The seer is told to shut up and seal the vision/book until the end; Every nation has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed by an hour; The heedless are like cattle, or even more astray; God's plotting (makr / kayd) outwits the schemers; none is safe from it but the losers; Defense of the prophet: there is no madness (jinna) in your companion; he is only a warner; and 2 more.

matches.note: Both reject an appeal to the fathers' sin: a-fa-tuhlikunā bi-mā faʿala l-mubṭilūn (our fathers associated others with God) vs ʾābôt yōʾkᵉlû bōser wᵉšinnê habbānîm tiqhênāh, answered by bēn lōʾ-yiśśāʾ baʿăwōn hāʾāb. In Ezek the sons complain that they suffer for their fathers; in Q they would plead their fathers to excuse their own idolatry.

passages.text: מַה לָּכֶ֗ם אַתֶּם֙ מֹֽשְׁלִים֙ אֶת הַמָּשָׁ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה עַל אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה
הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב וְאָב֙ לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הַבֵּ֔ן צִדְקַ֤ת הַצַּדִּיק֙ עָלָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְרִשְׁעַ֥ת רשע הָרָשָׁ֖ע עָלָ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה
أَوْ تَقُولُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَشْرَكَ ءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِّنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ

leads.title: Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain ↔ The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings (weight 6.7); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 12.3.

Only in Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain: 'You were an anointed guardian cherub; I placed you on the holy mountain of God'; The being was blameless from the day he was created until iniquity was found in him; God brings out a fire from within the sinner that consumes him and turns him to ashes on the ground; A primal figure was in Eden, the garden of God, covered with every precious stone (sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, emerald) and gold settings prepared on the day of his creation; The king of Tyre is called 'the seal of perfection (hotem toknit), full of wisdom and perfect in beauty'; The primal being walked among the 'stones of fire' on God's mountain; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; A city or king claims or is called 'perfect in beauty' (kelilat yofi); By wisdom and trade the ruler amasses gold and silver and his heart grows proud because of his wealth; The breastpiece of judgment set with twelve gems in four rows; A mountain called the mountain of God; Land near paradise rich in gold and precious stones; and 3 more.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

matches.label: God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings
matches.note: A being in God's garden is cast down for pride. Ezek: ʾatt-kərûv ... bə-har qōdeš ʾĕlōhîm hāyîtā bə-tôkh ʾavnê-ʾēš hithallākhtā ... gāvah libbəkhā ... ʿal-ʾereṣ hišlakhtîkhā. Q: anā khayrun minhu khalaqtanī min nārin ... fa-hbiṭ minhā fa-mā yakūnu laka an tatakabbara fīhā fa-khruj innaka mina l-ṣāghirīna. Both have fire (ʾavnê-ʾēš / min nār), pride (gāvah libbəkhā / tatakabbara) and being thrown down. In Ezek it is a lament over the king of Tyre; Q tells it as the fall of Iblis.

passages.text: אַ֨תְּ כְּר֔וּב מִמְשַׁ֖ח הַסּוֹכֵ֑ךְ וּנְתַתִּ֗יךָ בְּהַ֨ר קֹ֤דֶשׁ אֱלֹהִים֙ הָיִ֔יתָ בְּת֥וֹךְ אַבְנֵי אֵ֖שׁ הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ
בְּרֹ֣ב רְכֻלָּתְךָ֗ מָל֧וּ תוֹכְךָ֛ חָמָ֖ס וַֽתֶּחֱטָ֑א וָאֶחַלֶּלְךָ֩ מֵהַ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֤ים וָֽאַבֶּדְךָ֙ כְּר֣וּב הַסֹּכֵ֔ךְ מִתּ֖וֹךְ אַבְנֵי אֵֽשׁ
גָּבַ֤הּ לִבְּךָ֙ בְּיָפְיֶ֔ךָ שִׁחַ֥תָּ חָכְמָתְךָ֖ עַל יִפְעָתֶ֑ךָ עַל אֶ֣רֶץ הִשְׁלַכְתִּ֗יךָ לִפְנֵ֧י מְלָכִ֛ים נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְרַ֥אֲוָה בָֽךְ
قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
قَالَ ٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًا مَّدْحُورًا لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

leads.title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Creation is completed in six days (weight 5.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7). Pair score 16.6.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; and 25 more.

Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts]; God makes the night cover the day; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

matches.label: Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it
matches.note: What follows the six days. Gen: wa-ykhullû haš-šāmayim wə-hā-ʾāreṣ ... wa-yyišbōt bay-yôm haš-šəvîʿî, God rests and blesses the seventh day. Q: khalaqa l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa fī sittati ayyāmin thumma stawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi yughshī l-layla l-nahāra. The six days are kept, but in place of the rest God sits on the throne and goes on governing. There is no seventh day. cf. Q 50:38, where no weariness touches him.

passages.text: וַיְכֻלּ֛וּ הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ וְכָל צְבָאָֽם
וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה
וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת י֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֽׂוֹת

إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ يُغْشِى ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطْلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثًا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتٍۭ بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلْخَلْقُ وَٱلْأَمْرُ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

וְלִמְשֹׁל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה וּֽלֲהַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֣ין הַחֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי טֽוֹב

leads.title: War of the four kings, rescue of Lot, Melchizedek ↔ Hud and the people of Ad
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Ancient giant or Rephaite peoples (Rephaim, Zuzim, Emim, Horites) defeated (weight 5.1). Pair score 5.1.

Only in War of the four kings, rescue of Lot, Melchizedek: Valley full of bitumen pits into which fleeing kings fall; The patriarch's trained men number 318; Patriarch pursues captors with a small force and rescues his kinsman; Hero refuses to take spoils, not even a thread or sandal strap; Four eastern kings make war against five kings of the plain; Oath sworn by raising the hand to God; A tenth of everything given to a priest; A priest-king of Salem brings bread and wine and blesses the patriarch; God Most High (El Elyon), creator/possessor of heaven and earth.

Only in Hud and the people of Ad: False gods are only names the people and their fathers invented, with no authority from God; The people of Ad are given increased stature (bastatan fi l-khalq); Other nations displaced earlier peoples just as Israel will (Horites, Avvim by Caphtorim); God cuts off the last remnant (root, dabir) of a people who denied; A people of great stature is destroyed and cut off at the root; A later people (Ad, then Thamud) are made successors on the earth after a destroyed people; People marvel that a reminder came through a man from among them; Prophet calls himself his people's sincere and trustworthy adviser (nasih amin); The chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him'; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; The first man names the animals; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

matches.label: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden
matches.note: Gen: mik-kōl ʿēṣ-hag-gān ʾākhōl tōʾkhēl û-mēʿēṣ ha-ddaʿat ṭôv wā-rāʿ lōʾ tōʾkhal mimmennû kî bə-yôm ʾăkhālkhā mimmennû môt tāmût. Q: fa-kulā min ḥaythu shiʾtumā wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi l-shajarata fa-takūnā mina l-ẓālimīna. The open permission is kept; the threat of death becomes 'you will be among the wrongdoers', and the tree is nameless.

matches.label: How the first human's mate is made from the first human
matches.note: The mate made out of the first human: khalaqakum min nafsin wāḥidatin wa-jaʿala minhā zawjahā li-yaskuna ilayhā vs wayyiqqaḥ ʾaḥat miṣṣalʿōtāyw ... wayyiben ... ʾet-haṣṣēlāʿ ... lᵉʾiššāh. Q has no rib (ṣēlāʿ), no sleep (tardēmāh) and no named man: the mate comes 'from it', the one soul. The purpose is rest with her (li-yaskuna ilayhā), not ʿēzer kᵉnegdô against being alone.

matches.label: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit
matches.note: A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). There is no serpent and no curse to crawl on the belly (Gen 3:14).

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן
כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

matches.label: The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals
matches.note: What the tempter promises. Gen: wi-hyîtem kē-ʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôv wā-rāʿ, and God himself confirms the danger: hēn hā-ʾādām hāyāh kə-ʾaḥad mimmennû ... wā-ḥay lə-ʿōlām. Q: mā nahākumā rabbukumā ʿan hādhihi l-shajarati illā an takūnā malakayni aw takūnā mina l-khālidīna. 'Like gods knowing good and evil' becomes 'angels or immortals', a lie (bi-ghurūrin). Q has no divine admission that the humans have become 'like one of us'.

passages.text: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה פֶּן יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

matches.label: Which of the first couple is tempted and eats first
matches.note: Who is tempted and eats first. Gen: the serpent talks to the woman (wa-yyōʾmer ʾel-hā-ʾiššāh), she eats first and gives to her husband (wat-tittēn gam-lə-ʾîšāh ʿimmāh wa-yyōʾkhal). Q uses the dual throughout: wa-zawjuka ... fa-kulā ... wa-lā taqrabā ... waswasa lahumā ... fa-lammā dhāqā l-shajarata. The couple acts together and the woman is not singled out.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל הַנָּחָ֑שׁ מִפְּרִ֥י עֵֽץ הַגָּ֖ן נֹאכֵֽל
וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל
وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?'
matches.note: God's question. Gen: the couple hide (wa-yyitḥabbēʾ hā-ʾādām wə-ʾištô), God walks in the garden and calls ʾayyekkāh, then ha-min-hā-ʿēṣ ... ʾākhāltā. Q: wa-nādāhumā rabbuhumā a-lam anhakumā ʿan tilkumā l-shajarati wa-aqul lakumā inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduwwun mubīnun. No hiding and no walking God; the question is a reminder of a warning given.

passages.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing
matches.note: The decisive reversal. Gen: hā-ʾiššāh ʾăšer nātattāh ʿimmādî hiwʾ nātənāh-llî; han-nāḥāš hiššîʾanî, the man blames the woman (and God), the woman the serpent. Q: qālā rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā wa-in lam taghfir lanā wa-tarḥamnā la-nakūnanna mina l-khāsirīna. Both confess together and ask forgiveness. Blame-shifting gives way to joint repentance, and the blame-shifter in Q is Iblis (fa-bi-mā aghwaytanī, 7:16).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה לִּ֥י מִן הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל
قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

matches.label: Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck
matches.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). There are no curses on the woman (childbirth, 3:16) or the ground (3:17-19).

passages.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again)
matches.note: Gen: ʿad šûvəkhā ʾel-hā-ʾădāmāh kî mimmennāh luqqāḥtā kî-ʿāfār ʾattāh wə-ʾel-ʿāfār tāšûv, from dust and back to dust, as a curse. Q: fīhā taḥyawna wa-fīhā tamūtūna wa-minhā tukhrajūna. Q adds the third step, resurrection from the earth.

passages.text: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ

matches.label: First humans expelled from the garden
matches.note: Gen: wa-yšalləḥēhû ... wa-ygāreš ʾet-hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and the flaming sword guarding the tree of life, lest he eat and live forever. Q: ihbiṭū ... wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīnin. A descent to a temporary home, with no guard, no tree of life and no fear of human immortality.

passages.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם
וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן עֵ֜דֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Fig leaves sewn into coverings
matches.note: Gen: wat-tippāqaḥnāh ʿênê šənêhem wa-yyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wa-yyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnāh. Q: badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-jannati. Both sew leaves, but in Q they are 'leaves of the garden' (no fig), and Q says the nakedness 'appeared' rather than 'their eyes were opened'.

passages.text: וַתִּפָּקַ֨חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden
matches.note: Gen 3:3, the woman's paraphrase: wə-lōʾ tiggəʿû bô, 'nor touch it', a fence God had not said. Q, God's own command: wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi l-shajarata, 'do not come near'. The tree is unnamed in Q (no 'knowledge of good and evil').

passages.text: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן תְּמֻתֽוּן
وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked

leads.title: The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes ↔ The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it (weight 6.7); Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell (weight 5.0). Pair score 11.7.

Only in The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes: The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations; Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness; The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint; 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)'; A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor; The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork; The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come; Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it; The earth will be full of the knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea; Peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for nothing; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; God asks Gehenna 'Are you full?' and it answers 'Are there any more?'; and 6 more.

Only in The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols: A couple vow thanks for a sound child, then ascribe partners to God in what he gave; Those you call on besides God are servants like yourselves; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Parents' words to God about the child he gave them [divergence between the texts]; Taunt: do the idols have feet to walk, hands to grasp, eyes to see, ears to hear?; Likeness between the idols and those who call on them [divergence between the texts]; Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps; Humankind is created from a single soul, from which its mate was made to dwell with it; The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it.

leads.title: YHWH's lawsuit; priests, divination and cultic harlotry ↔ Hell's quarrels, the camel and the needle, the people of the Heights
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in YHWH's lawsuit; priests, divination and cultic harlotry: Men sacrifice with qedeshot (cult women) and go aside with harlots; Prophet lists violations echoing the Decalogue: swearing, lying, murder, theft, adultery; 'Like people, like priest': both punished alike; My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; the priest who rejected knowledge is rejected; Israel is like a stubborn heifer; YHWH brings a lawsuit (riv) against his people; The people consult their piece of wood and their staff (rhabdomancy) gives them oracles; Priests feed on the people's sin and set their heart on their iniquity; A 'spirit of harlotry' (ruah zenunim) leads the people astray; Because of sin the land mourns and beasts, birds and even fish of the sea perish; Bethel ('house of God') mocked as Beth-aven ('house of iniquity'); Pagan worship on high mountains, hills and under every green tree.

Only in Hell's quarrels, the camel and the needle, the people of the Heights: A partition (hijab) separates paradise from hell; Impossibility proverb: entering paradise is as possible as a camel (or rope) passing through the eye of a needle; The damned ask for intercessors or to be sent back to do differently; The damned beg the blessed to pour some water on them and are refused; Each nation entering hell curses its sister nation; The people of paradise and the people of hell call out to each other across the divide; The gates of heaven are not opened for those who arrogantly deny the signs; Hell is the damned's bed below and covering above; A herald proclaims between paradise and hell: God's curse is on the wrongdoers; Men on the heights (al-A'raf) between paradise and hell recognize all by their marks, hoping to enter; The damned find no intercessors to plead for them; Paradise is given to the blessed as an inheritance for what they did; and 4 more.

leads.title: Judgment on priests and kings; 'on the third day he will raise us' ↔ Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 4.4.

Only in Judgment on priests and kings; 'on the third day he will raise us': God is like a moth (or pus) to Ephraim and like rot to Judah; God returns to his place until the people acknowledge guilt and seek his face; 'Like Adam they transgressed the covenant'; The people's love is like a morning cloud and the dew that vanishes early; 'I desire steadfast love (hesed) and not sacrifice, knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings'; A band of priests murders on the road to Shechem; 'After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up'; Ephraim sees its sickness and goes to the great king of Assyria, who cannot heal it; The leaders have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread on Tabor; Blow the shofar in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah, sound the alarm at Beth-aven; God is like a lion that tears its prey and carries it off with none to rescue; A 'spirit of harlotry' (ruah zenunim) leads the people astray; and 2 more.

Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts]; God makes the night cover the day; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons.

leads.title: No rejoicing for Israel; exile, the mad prophet, Baal-peor ↔ Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 answers the other.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The charge that a prophet is mad [response between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in No rejoicing for Israel; exile, the mad prophet, Baal-peor: The apostasy at Baal-peor; Their sacrifices are like the bread of mourners: all who eat it are defiled; Prayer/curse: 'Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts'; In exile (Assyria) they will eat unclean food; Israel loves a harlot's hire on every threshing floor of grain; God found Israel like grapes in the wilderness, like the first fig; Egypt gathers them and Memphis (Moph) buries them; thorns in their tents; 'The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad'; Israel's sin recalled as 'the days of Gibeah'; God appoints the prophet as a watchman (tsofeh) for the house of Israel; Punishment is a return to Egypt (reversal of the exodus); Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

Only in Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour: God has created many jinn and humans for hell; The charge that a prophet is mad; Having eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, said of idols or of people [divergence between the texts]; God leads deniers step by step to ruin and grants them respite (istidraj); The prophet disclaims knowledge of the unseen and power over benefit or harm; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; To God belong the most beautiful names; call on him by them; The seer is told to shut up and seal the vision/book until the end; Every nation has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed by an hour; The heedless are like cattle, or even more astray; God's plotting (makr / kayd) outwits the schemers; none is safe from it but the losers; Defense of the prophet: there is no madness (jinna) in your companion; he is only a warner; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The heedless are like cattle, or even more astray (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city: City or people given a new name in the future age (e.g. 'City of Righteousness', 'Hephzibah'); The faithful city has become a harlot; silver turned to dross, wine diluted with water; Worshippers shamed by the sacred oaks (elim) and gardens they chose; God will smelt away the dross of his people as in a furnace to purify them; Daughter Zion left alone like a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field, a besieged city; Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores; Sky and earth 'listen to their Lord' (adhinat) and are made to obey at the end; Israel likened to a donkey that knows, or does not understand, what it has [divergence between the texts]; Prophet addresses his own rulers and people as 'Sodom' and 'Gomorrah'; In Lot's town only one house of submitters (muslimin) was found, and the believers were brought out; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); Book or oracle opens with a heading naming the prophet, his father and the kings in whose days he saw the vision; and 12 more.

Only in Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour: God has created many jinn and humans for hell; The charge that a prophet is mad; The charge that a prophet is mad [response between the texts]; Having eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, said of idols or of people [divergence between the texts]; God leads deniers step by step to ruin and grants them respite (istidraj); The prophet disclaims knowledge of the unseen and power over benefit or harm; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; To God belong the most beautiful names; call on him by them; The seer is told to shut up and seal the vision/book until the end; Every nation has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed by an hour; God's plotting (makr / kayd) outwits the schemers; none is safe from it but the losers; Defense of the prophet: there is no madness (jinna) in your companion; he is only a warner; and 2 more.

leads.title: Bel and Nebo carried off; God who carries Israel ↔ The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in Bel and Nebo carried off; God who carries Israel: Babylon's gods Bel and Nebo bow and stoop, their images loaded as burdens on weary beasts; God summons a bird of prey from the east, the man of his counsel (the conqueror Cyrus); God alone announces the end from the beginning and proves his deity by predictions fulfilled; Idols must be carried by their worshipers, whereas God has carried his people from the womb to old age; Satirical description of an idol being made by craftsmen from gold, silver, metal or wood, then carried and set up; Cult images are carried off by raiders or a migrating group; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped'; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols: A couple vow thanks for a sound child, then ascribe partners to God in what he gave; Those you call on besides God are servants like yourselves; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Parents' words to God about the child he gave them [divergence between the texts]; Taunt: do the idols have feet to walk, hands to grasp, eyes to see, ears to hear?; Likeness between the idols and those who call on them [divergence between the texts]; Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps; Humankind is created from a single soul, from which its mate was made to dwell with it; Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell.

leads.title: Second servant song - called from the womb, a light to the nations ↔ The unlettered prophet foretold in Torah and Gospel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The messenger is sent to all humankind (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Second servant song - called from the womb, a light to the nations: Exiles return from far lands including the land of Sinim (later read as China); God makes the servant's mouth a sharp sword and hides him as a polished arrow in his quiver; Prisoners and those in darkness are told 'Go out' and set free; The servant complains he has labored in vain and spent his strength for nothing; The servant of God is addressed as 'Israel', in whom God will be glorified; Kings and princes rise, bow or shut their mouths before the once despised servant; The servant or God's teaching is made a light to the nations, salvation to the end of the earth; God calls, forms, knows or consecrates his servant or prophet from the womb, before birth; God levels mountains and builds a highway in the wilderness for the returning exiles.

Only in The unlettered prophet foretold in Torah and Gospel: The new prophet removes the burdens and fetters (isr, aghlal) laid on the earlier community; God lifts a yoke or burden from his people [divergence between the texts]; Which foods God permits and which he forbids [divergence between the texts]; A future prophet promised in the earlier scripture [response between the texts]; The coming prophet is found written in the Torah and the Gospel; The awaited messenger is 'the unlettered prophet' (al-nabi al-ummi); God will raise up a prophet like Moses from among the brothers and put his words in his mouth; I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal; there is no god beside me.

leads.title: The remnant asks for an oracle, rejects it and drags Jeremiah to Tahpanhes; stones hidden in the pavement ↔ Salih, Thamud and the she-camel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet reminds a disobedient people that he delivered God's message (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The remnant asks for an oracle, rejects it and drags Jeremiah to Tahpanhes; stones hidden in the pavement: The conqueror will burn the temples of a foreign land's gods; The remnant seeks safety in Egypt, where they think they will see no war nor hunger; God says he repents (nihamti) of the evil he did to his people; The conqueror breaks the obelisks (matsevot) of Beth-shemesh/Heliopolis in Egypt; The prophet's answer from God comes only after ten days; The people ask the prophet to pray for them and to tell them God's word; The people swear to obey whatever God answers, then reject the oracle; Opponents tell the prophet 'You are lying; God did not send you'; The prophet is taken down to Egypt against his counsel by the fleeing remnant; The conqueror will wrap (or pick clean) Egypt as a shepherd does his garment; The prophet buries large stones in the pavement at Pharaoh's palace where the conqueror will set his throne; The sword and famine they fear will overtake them in the very place they flee to; and 1 more.

Only in Salih, Thamud and the she-camel: The arrogant elite confront the weak (mustad'afun) who believed the prophet; The prophet turns from his destroyed people: 'I conveyed the message and advised you'; A later people (Ad, then Thamud) are made successors on the earth after a destroyed people; A people is destroyed by an earthquake/tremor (al-rajfa); A people carve houses out of the mountains and build palaces on the plains; Prophet calls himself his people's sincere and trustworthy adviser (nasih amin); The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him'.

leads.title: Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test ↔ The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans (weight 6.7); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.5.

Only in Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test: The verb 'bless' (barekh) used as a scribal euphemism for cursing God; Grown sons hold feasts in turn, each on his day, and invite their sisters; A great wind from the desert strikes the four corners of the house and it falls on the feasting children; God has set a protective hedge around the righteous man, his house and goods; 'Fire of God' falls from heaven and consumes flocks and servants; Messenger after messenger arrives while the last is still speaking, each the sole survivor of a disaster; 'I alone escaped to tell you'; 'Does he fear God for nothing?': piety suspected of being motivated by reward; The exemplary righteous man is a non-Israelite living in the land of Uz in the east; Father offers burnt offerings in case his children 'blessed' (cursed) God in their hearts; A blessed man has seven sons and three daughters; Mourner shaves his head and falls to the ground; and 19 more.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Job - 'man born of woman'; the tree has hope: 'Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one'; The dead man does not know whether his sons are honored or brought low; As waters wear away stones and mountains crumble, so God destroys human hope; Man's days are determined; God has set limits he cannot pass; Sufferer wishes God would hide him in Sheol until his anger passes and then remember him; 'If a man dies, will he live again?': hope of a release (chalifah) after hard service; Transgressions sealed up in a bag (tseror) and iniquity plastered over; The dead will not wake until the heavens are no more; 'Man born of woman is of few days and full of trouble'; he comes forth like a flower and withers; Death as final, voiced by a sufferer or by deniers of resurrection [divergence between the texts]; Human life on earth is hard service (tsava), its days like those of a hired laborer; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise; and 2 more.

Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; God makes the night cover the day; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֞ף שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֹתָ֖ם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הָאֹֽהֶל

leads.title: Obadiah's vision against Edom's pride ↔ Salih, Thamud and the she-camel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A people carve houses out of the mountains and build palaces on the plains (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Obadiah's vision against Edom's pride: A nation's treaty partners and table companions deceive and overpower it; An envoy is sent among the nations to summon them to battle; Grape-gatherers would leave gleanings and thieves take only enough, but God strips the nation bare; Is there no longer wisdom in Teman (Edom)?; Edom dwells in the clefts of the rock (sela) and thinks no one can bring it down; The proud one who builds his nest high as the eagle or among the stars is brought down by God; Brief oracles against neighboring nations (Amalek, Kenite, Asshur, Kittim).

Only in Salih, Thamud and the she-camel: The arrogant elite confront the weak (mustad'afun) who believed the prophet; The prophet reminds a disobedient people that he delivered God's message; The prophet turns from his destroyed people: 'I conveyed the message and advised you'; A later people (Ad, then Thamud) are made successors on the earth after a destroyed people; A people is destroyed by an earthquake/tremor (al-rajfa); Prophet calls himself his people's sincere and trustworthy adviser (nasih amin); The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him'.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God makes the night cover the day (weight 6.3); God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 20.9.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.

Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts]; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh).

leads.title: Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus ↔ Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The dust of the earth becomes lice on man and beast (weight 6.3); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 6.0); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 5.6); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.6); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 46.5.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 25 more.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

matches.label: A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus
matches.note: A short plague list. Q: fa-arsalnā ʿalayhimu l-ṭūfāna wa-l-jarāda wa-l-qummala wa-l-ḍafādiʿa wa-l-dama āyātin mufaṣṣalātin, five plagues. Ps 105: hāfakh ʾet-mêmêhem lə-dām ... šāraṣ ʾarṣām ṣəfardəʿîm ... ʿārōv kinnîm ... ʾarbeh. Q's last three, qummal, ḍafādiʿ, dam (lice, frogs, blood), are Exodus's first three (dām, ṣəfardəʿîm, kinnîm) in reverse order. Q adds ṭūfān, which is in no HB list, and leaves out the death of the firstborn (Ps 105:36).

فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلْجَرَادَ وَٱلْقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتٍ مُّفَصَّلَٰتٍ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا مُّجْرِمِينَ

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 31 more.

leads.title: Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile ↔ The lowing calf and the seventy
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses 'stood in the breach' (pérets) before God to turn back his wrath from destroying the people (weight 6.7); The people exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass (weight 6.7); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 4.7). Only in Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile: Israel ate 'sacrifices of the dead' (zivhei metim) at Baal-peor; God caused the exiles to be pitied by all their captors; God grants the people's wilderness craving but sends wasting (razon) into their souls; Provoked at Meribah, Moses spoke rashly with his lips and suffered because of the people; Phinehas's intervention 'was reckoned to him as righteousness for all generations'; Israel 'yokes itself' to Baal of Peor; List of punishment types for the nations: stone-storm, the Shout, swallowing by the earth, drowning; Speaker confesses personal sin and pleads for forgiveness and cleansing; God turned the sea into dry land and they crossed the river on foot; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; A closing doxology and the divine title it uses [divergence between the texts]; Egypt is called 'the tents of Ham' or 'the land of Ham'; and 14 more.

Only in The lowing calf and the seventy: Aaron pleads 'son of my mother, the people overpowered me and almost killed me'; The angry prophet seizes his brother by the head (and beard), dragging him; The seventy chosen men are seized by a tremor at the appointed meeting; When his anger subsides the prophet takes up the cast-down tablets again, their text intact; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; Moses intercedes for Aaron, with whom God was angry enough to destroy him; God's mercy encompasses all things; Moses includes himself with the guilty people in his plea after the calf [divergence between the texts]; Moses prays for Aaron after the calf [divergence between the texts]; After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 6.0); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 5.6); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 27.9.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 36 more.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

leads.title: The final day on the Mount of Olives; living waters; Sukkot for the nations ↔ Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Knowledge of the Hour is with God alone; it will come suddenly (weight 5.0). Pair score 5.0.

Only in The final day on the Mount of Olives; living waters; Sukkot for the nations: A unique day known to YHWH, neither day nor night, without light, cold and frost; at evening there will be light; The great earthquake in the days of King Uzziah is remembered as a reference point; Plague on Jerusalem's attackers: their flesh, eyes and tongues rot while they stand on their feet; In that day 'Holy to YHWH' is inscribed on the horses' bells and every pot in Jerusalem becomes holy; The whole land is leveled like the Arabah while Jerusalem is raised up on its site; Living waters flow out from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, summer and winter; God's feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits east to west into a great valley, half moving north and half south; God gathers all nations to battle against Jerusalem: the city is taken, houses plundered, women raped, half exiled; Survivors of the nations go up yearly to Jerusalem to bow to the King, YHWH of hosts, and keep the feast of Booths; Families of the earth that do not go up for Sukkot get no rain; Egypt is struck with plague; There will no longer be a Canaanite (trader) in the house of YHWH; YHWH comes and all the holy ones (angels) with him; and 10 more.

Only in Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour: God has created many jinn and humans for hell; The charge that a prophet is mad; The charge that a prophet is mad [response between the texts]; Having eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, said of idols or of people [divergence between the texts]; God leads deniers step by step to ruin and grants them respite (istidraj); The prophet disclaims knowledge of the unseen and power over benefit or harm; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; To God belong the most beautiful names; call on him by them; The seer is told to shut up and seal the vision/book until the end; Every nation has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed by an hour; The heedless are like cattle, or even more astray; God's plotting (makr / kayd) outwits the schemers; none is safe from it but the losers; and 2 more.

leads.title: Adam, the angels and Iblis ↔ The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: First humans expelled from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 41.2.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; The first man names the animals; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 15 more.

leads.title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 28.2.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 17 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay (weight 6.3); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 34.4.

sides.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). There are no curses on the woman (childbirth, 3:16) or the ground (3:17-19).

passages.text: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

Gen's enmity is between serpent and woman and their seed, and the way back is barred by cherubim. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

sides.note: A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ إِلَّآ أَنْ ءَامَنَّا بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَآءَتْنَا رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ يَٰقَوْمِ إِن كُنتُمْ ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ فَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلُوٓا۟ إِن كُنتُم مُّسْلِمِينَ
فَقَالُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَنَجِّنَا بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

sides.note: 'do not make us a trial for the wrongdoers'

matches.label: The meek / those who wait for YHWH / the righteous and their seed shall inherit the land (yirshu arets)

passages.text: قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱصْبِرُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ يُورِثُهَا مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلْعَٰقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ

وَأَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُوا۟ يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشَٰرِقَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَغَٰرِبَهَا ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟ وَدَمَّرْنَا مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُۥ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْرِشُونَ

sides.note: the earth is God's; he gives it to whom he wills; the oppressed inherit east and west of the blessed land

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ وَرَزَقْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ فَمَا ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِى بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا۟ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ

sides.note: settled in a sound abode

matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest

passages.text: قَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَأَرْسِلْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَٰحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ
وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ٱئْتُونِى بِكُلِّ سَٰحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
فَلَمَّآ أَلْقَوْا۟ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ مَا جِئْتُم بِهِ ٱلسِّحْرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَيُبْطِلُهُۥٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُصْلِحُ عَمَلَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

matches.label: The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people

passages.text: وَقَالُوا۟ مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِۦ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ لِّتَسْحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلْجَرَادَ وَٱلْقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتٍ مُّفَصَّلَٰتٍ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا مُّجْرِمِينَ

sides.note: self-arrogance rather than divine hardening

passages.text: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ ءَاتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُۥ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَٰلًا فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِكَ رَبَّنَا ٱطْمِسْ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَٱشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ

sides.note: at Moses' own prayer

matches.label: The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives

passages.text: فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُوا۟ عَنْهَا غَٰفِلِينَ

sides.note: al-yamm

passages.text: وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتْ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓا۟ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

leads.title: Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues ↔ Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians
leads.summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron (weight 6.3); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents (weight 6.0); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.6); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 45.6.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes; Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life'; Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?'; and 3 more.
